_comment: Image-to-3D on the user's ComfyUI with Pixal3D (TencentARC, SIGGRAPH 2026: TRELLIS.2's backbone with pixel-aligned conditioning, so the geometry follows the input view), ComfyUI's native nodes (0.38+): a GLB mesh from one concept image. Shape only, no texture: VECTOR's hologram bake keeps geometry and feature edges. The graph is the shape half of Comfy-Org's template (3d_pixal3d_trellis2_image_to_model): the subject is masked in the graph (Lucida, in place of the template's BiRefNet) and cropped to its mask with a 10% margin, MoGe-2 estimates the view's horizontal field of view for the conditioning; structure 12 steps (cfg 7.5, CFG override to 1 after 66.7%, rescale 0.7, shift 5), shape 20 steps and the upsample to 1536 12 steps (cfg 7.5, override after 76.9%, rescale 0.5). The decoded shape is remeshed as the template does (dual contouring of its distance field at 768, 20 smoothing passes) but keeping only the outer shell and dropping specks (the bake's feature edges would trace every loose fragment and an inner shell), then decimated to at most 500k faces (the bake takes it to its own budget). Pixal3D builds the object in the concept's camera frame, so a concept seen from above comes out leaning back by the camera's elevation: _meta.level has bromigos art stand the saved GLB up (glb.rs: the pitch that squares its surfaces, applied when it clearly helps). Weights: diffusion_models/pixal3d_int8_convrot, vae/trellis_2_shape_vae_bf16, clip_vision/dino_v3_L_naf_fp32 (Comfy-Org/Pixal3D), geometry_estimation/moge_2_vitl_normal_fp16 (Comfy-Org/MoGe), background_removal/lucida_v7 (egeorcun/lucida); helm/comfyui in the homelab repo fetches them.

_meta.vram_note: ComfyUI's peak on the 5090 (32 GiB, the voice and embeddings servers resident: 13.9 GiB at rest), a 1536 px concept, measured 2026-10-09; ComfyUI loads each stage's model as it needs it
_meta.seconds_note: a 1536 px concept on the 5090, the models loaded cold, 35 to 57 s: the three samplers, the decode, the remesh (about 10 s), the decimation and the levelling
